title: Deciphering the limitations of immortalized hepatocyte cell lines for the study of liver cis-regulatory elements
summary: Background: Immortalized cell lines are widely used to study transcriptional regulation. However, previous studies have shown that immortalization and prolonged culture can alter their regulatory landscapes, potentially compromising their ability to model native cis-regulatory element (CRE) activity. Hepatocyte-like cell lines (HLCs), particularly HepG2, are frequently used to study liver CREs, but whether non-cancer-derived HLCs, such as AML12, better recapitulate native regulatory landscapes remains unclear. Furthermore, cell culture conditions have been shown to influence gene expression and CRE activity, raising the possibility that optimizing culture conditions could improve HLC gene regulatory similarities to primary liver tissue. Together, these questions highlight the importance of characterizing the transcriptional regulatory landscapes of HLCs and evaluating the effects of culture conditions when using these cell lines to study native liver CRE activity. Results: We systematically characterized the molecular features and transcriptional regulatory landscapes of four HLCs and compared them with those of liver tissue. We examined AML12 cells using RT-qPCR and flow cytometry and found that they express some hepatocyte markers but lack key characteristics of mature hepatocytes. We then used ATAC-seq to characterize the chromatin accessibility landscape of AML12. Through transcription factor motif enrichment, functional enrichment, and machine learning analyses, we found substantial differences in the cis-regulatory landscapes of AML12 and primary mouse liver. Modifying AML12 culture conditions altered some regulatory features but did not substantially improve their similarity to primary liver tissue. We then extended these analyses to three additional HLCs and found similar differences between their regulatory landscapes and that of primary liver tissue. Notably, HepG2 recapitulated native liver regulatory landscapes better than the tested non-cancer-derived cell lines. Conclusion: Our findings reveal substantial differences in transcriptional regulatory landscapes between immortalized HLCs and native liver tissue that persist despite modifications to culture conditions. These results highlight the limitations of HLCs in modeling native liver transcriptional regulation and emphasize the importance of evaluating their regulatory landscapes before using them to investigate CRE function. Keywords: Hepatocyte-like cell lines; Cis-regulatory elements; Liver; Cell culture conditions; ATAC-seq

title: Leveraging the largest harmonized epigenomic data collection for metadata prediction validated and augmented over 350,000 public epigenomic datasets
summary: Epigenomic data found in public databases often suffer from issues of non-standardization and incompleteness in their associated metadata. There are currently no automated approaches to validate or correct such missing or inaccurate metadata information. To tackle this challenge, we harnessed the extensive harmonized data and metadata provided by the EpiATLAS project of the International Human Epigenome Consortium (IHEC) to train EpiClass, a suite of machine learning classifiers that can predict key metadata (~98% accuracy), including experimental assay, donor sex, biospecimen source and sample cancer status. The development of these classifiers enabled the identification of a few mislabeled and low-quality datasets in the EpiATLAS project, while also completing with high-confidence most of the missing metadata. These classifiers were also validated on thousands of ENCODE datasets absent from the initial training, then applied to assess more than 350,000 human ChIP-seq and RNA-seq datasets from public repositories. Overall, this effort not only validated the accuracy of the vast majority of assays reported by the original authors, but also unveiled ~500 datasets with discrepancies, in particular through data swap during data entry. More importantly, EpiClass also supplied high-confidence predictions for over 320,000 metadata attributes of the biological sample such as the sex, cancer status and biomaterial type, which had been originally omitted in the majority of cases. Our work introduces the first systematic approach for metadata correction and augmentation, enhancing the quality and reliability of publicly available epigenomic data.

title: Machine Learning-based Transcriptomic Data Analysis of Long COVID Patients: Generating Hypotheses for Molecular Signatures
summary: Introduction: Long COVID (LC) remains a global public-health challenge, affecting an estimated 10-30% of COVID-19-survivors. Machine learning (ML) can help identify molecular features associated with LC. Human ion channels (HICs), that regulate immune-cell signaling and cellular homeostasis, may contribute to LC-associated processes and offer insights into relevant pathways and potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methodology: RNA-seq data from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients across six datasets were integrated, preprocessed, and corrected for batch effects. Supervised ML models were evaluated using leave-one-batch-out validation, with SHAP identifying features across validation folds. Functional enrichment, host-host and host-viral protein-protein interaction analyses were performed, followed by drug interaction analysis of potential HICs within the resulting interactome. Results: A support vector classifier with an RBF kernel achieved a mean-AUC of 0.664 across six validation folds. SHAP analysis of the three selected folds (AUC = 0.722, 0.836, and 0.817) identified 225, 153, and 241 genes, respectively. Functional enrichment highlighted pathways including histidine metabolism and TNF signaling. Among the 613 genes identified across these folds, 9 were HICs and 39 were immune signaling-related genes (ISGs), whose protein-protein interaction analysis revealed a pharmacologically relevant interactome. Furthermore, four HICs including CLCN3, KCNQ3, RYR1, and ZACN interacted with 30 approved drugs. Conclusion: ML-based analysis of integrated RNA-seq data identified HICs and ISGs associated with LC, while functional enrichment and PPI analyses provided insights into their potential biological relevance. Drug interaction analysis further highlighted candidate HIC-targeting drugs for future investigation in LC management. This computational framework provides preliminary, hypothesis-generating insights to guide future research.

title: Machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory metagenomes
summary: Background: Targeted therapy for patients with suspected respiratory infections traditionally requires bacterial culture followed by phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), a process that can take up to 5 days. In acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), delays in identifying the causative pathogen and its resistance profile may be especially harmful because patients are critically ill and often receive broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics. The growing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) further complicates clinical decision-making by reducing effective treatment options and increasing the risk of inadequate initial therapy. Culture-free, AI-driven computational metagenomic strategies have the potential to drastically shorten this window, enabling more rapid targeted therapy prescription. To show the feasibility of such approaches, we develop a proof-of-concept framework based on clinical metagenomics. Methods: We simulated respiratory metagenomes using real-world bacterial genomes with associated antimicrobial susceptibility phenotypes. Each simulated metagenome contained a fixed commensal background and one clinically important respiratory pathogen, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Pseudomonas aeruginosa, at 5% or 10% bacterial read abundance. Realistic reads were simulated for Oxford Nanopore, PacBio, and Illumina sequencing platforms. Random Forest (RF) classifiers were trained and evaluated using five-fold, strain-grouped cross-validation with fold-specific {chi}2-ranked 13-mer features. ResFinder and KARGA were included as reference-based metagenomics benchmarks and evaluated using the same five held-out folds across the three sequencing platforms and two pathogen-abundance conditions. Results: RF performance varied substantially across species, antibiotics, and sequencing platforms. The strongest and most consistent results were observed for K. pneumoniae, with accuracy reaching approximately 0.96 for ceftazidime, 0.93 for amikacin, and 0.92 for ciprofloxacin. Performance for P. aeruginosa was more heterogeneous: long-read models performed well for amikacin, reaching 0.89 with PacBio and 0.88 with Nanopore, whereas Illumina performed substantially better for ciprofloxacin, ceftazidime, and levofloxacin, reaching accuracies of approximately 0.87, 0.77, and 0.70, respectively. Across most organism-antibiotic combinations, RF accuracy was numerically higher than the classification accuracies obtained with KARGA and ResFinder, which generally remained near 0.50. Increasing pathogen abundance from 5% to 10% and increasing the number of selected features from 2,500 to 5,000 generally produced modest improvements in classification accuracy, although the magnitude of improvement varied across organism-antibiotic combinations and sequencing platforms. Conclusions: Genome-wide k-mer machine learning can recover phenotype-associated antimicrobial resistance signals from simulated respiratory metagenomes, although performance depends strongly on the organism, antibiotic, and sequencing platform. These results represent a simulation-based proof of concept.

title: Functional hot-spots and communication networks of the cellular prion protein from information-theoretical measures
summary: The cellular prion protein (PrPC) is a ~33 kDa molecule featuring a disordered region and a globular part, mostly expressed in the brain and in the central nervous system. The biological role of this protein is still unclear, but its pathogenic behavior in specific conditions has been ascertained. In fact, for reasons that are still under scrutiny, PrPC may convert to its misfolded counterpart PrPSc, which accumulates in tissues and gives rise to a plethora of neurodegenerative diseases. At this day, the mechanism underlying the misfolding process of PrPC to PrPSc is not fully understood. Here, we analyze molecular dynamics simulations of PrPC by means of information-theoretical approaches to single out specific residues that might play a key functional role in the protein, and to identify the network of communication that relays mechanical signals among distal regions of the molecule. We found such hot-spots in the alpha-I helix and the beta-II--alpha-II hinge, which are involved in the initiation of the misfolding process; furthermore, the pair Val209-Cys214 acts as the main link for the information relay between the two aforementioned regions. These observations suggest that the main determinants that trigger the pathogenic conformational transition of PrPC's globular domain are inherently encoded in its structure; this result opens the possibility of developing therapeutic molecules that interfere with these functional elements to mitigate the protein's misfolding and aggregation.

title: On the Importance of Polarizability in Simulations of 2D IR Spectra of the Potassium Ion Channel KcsA
summary: The bacterial KcsA channel is a K+ channel which is functionally homologous to mammalian ion channels. It assembles as a cone-shaped tetramer that is embedded in the membrane. Its narrowest conserved region, known as the selectivity filter (SF) is comprised of five distinct ion-binding sites (S0-S4) that coordinate the selective permeation of K+ ions. Recent two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy experiments, together with molecular dynamics and line shape simulations on the isotope-labeled SF residues V76 and G77, suggest that in the closed conductive state either S1/S3 or S2/S4 are occupied by ions with water molecules in between, consistent with the soft knock-on mechanism. 2D IR spectroscopy probes amide I vibrations that are highly sensitive to local environmental fluctuations thus providing a powerful approach for distinguishing ion permeation mechanisms. However, current 2D IR spectral calculations are largely restricted to non-polarizable force fields, which may not fully capture the realistic channel behavior. Here, we report 2D IR simulations based on all-atom molecular dynamics trajectories of the KcsA channel embedded in a lipid membrane performed using nonpolarizable CHARMM36m, polarizable CHARMM-Drude, and CHARMM force field with electronic continuum correction. The spectra were calculated for V76 and G77 isotope-labeled SF and for soft knock-on configurations. Our results show that simulations with the polarizable CHARMM-Drude force field better reproduce experimental 2D IR spectra underscoring the importance of including the polarization effects in simulations of ion channels.

title: Decoding Cortical Precursors of Evoked and Spontaneous Pupil Dilation
summary: Pupil dilation reflects arousal and occurs both in response to sensory events and spontaneously. However, whether these two forms of dilation are preceded by distinct cortical dynamics remains unclear. Here, we combined pupillometry, wide-field Ca2+; imaging in mice, and explainable machine learning to estimate cortical activity patterns that predict pupil dilation. Evoked dilation was examined during somatosensory, visual pattern, and visual context stimulations, and spontaneous dilation was analyzed using a public resting state dataset. Independent components of cortical activity were used as inputs to recurrent neural network (RNN) decoders. When sessions with pre-existing dilation were excluded, the decoders predicted evoked dilation above that of the shuffled-label controls. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) with spatial back mapping revealed that activity around the retrosplenial cortex contributed to predictions across sensory modalities, whereas secondary motor cortex activity was prominent specifically during visual stimulation. In contrast, spontaneous dilation required lower-frequency cortical signals for decoding and showed a reverse order, with medial anterior activity preceding retrosplenial and secondary motor contributions. These findings indicate that evoked and spontaneous pupil dilation are preceded by distinct cortical dynamics, with evoked dilation involving a retrosplenial signal shared across sensory modalities and subsequent recruitment of the secondary motor cortex during visual stimulation.

title: The ACDC domains of AP2-O3 and FD3 contribute to protein interactions and ookinete development
summary: The Apicomplexan AP2 (ApiAP2) family of transcription factors are key regulators of Plasmodium spp. parasite development. In addition to containing AP2 DNA-binding domains, nine ApiAP2 proteins also encode an apicomplexan-specific ACDC domain whose function remains largely unknown. Here, we dissect the biological role of the ACDC domain from two female-specific regulators, AP2-O3 and FD3, using the rodent malaria model Plasmodium yoelii and the human malaria parasite P. falciparum. In Plasmodium yoelii, deletion of the ACDC domain preserved AP2-O3 and FD3 protein presence and nuclear localization without significantly affecting asexual growth or gametocyte production. However, deletion of these domains impaired the gametocyte-to-ookinete transition, reducing ookinete conversion efficiency. Proteomic and biochemical studies indicate that the AP2-O3 ACDC domain interacts with FD3, while the FD3 ACDC domain preferentially associates with full-length FD3. Transcriptomic data showed that over 80% of transcripts that increased after FD3 ACDC deletion were also higher following AP2-O3 loss, with female gametocyte marker expression largely unchanged. In Plasmodium falciparum, removing the FD3 ACDC domain did not affect female lineage-specific expression of FD3, nuclear localization of FD3, or the asexual growth and gametocyte maturation of parasites. Leveraging the high sequence conservation of ACDC domains across the Plasmodium genus, we conducted structure-based virtual screening of 283 compounds targeting the predicted PfAP2-O3 and PfFD3 ACDC interaction interface. Seven compounds ranked among the top candidate inhibitors for both domains, and the highest-priority ligand for each domain was further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Collectively, our findings support a role for ACDC domains in ApiAP2 protein interactions and identify candidate compounds for future experimental evaluation as potential transmission-blocking leads.

title: Modeling Host-Virus Interactions of Avian Corona Virus Reveals Cytokine Feedback as a driver of Strain-Specific Immune Response
summary: The interplay between RNA viral dynamics and innate immunity remains poorly understood, mainly because RNA viruses trigger highly nonlinear cytokine responses. We address this using infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a major poultry pathogen, as a model system. We developed a set of mathematical models and compared those with experimental data from two IBV strains infecting chicken macrophages.By model fitting and supervised Machine Learning we reveal that positive feedback in interferon- production is essential to reproduce the dynamics of one IBV strain but likely absent in the other. We further provide strain-specific estimations of key parameters such as infection rates, production and decay rates of virus and cytokine levels. Notably, different strains produced distinctive cytokine profiles, highlighting feedback as a key determinant of strain-specific immune signatures. Our results establish a quantitative framework for dissecting host-virus interactions and uncover cytokine feedback as a generic yet underappreciated feature in models of RNA virus kinetics.

title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
summary: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%). Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF-enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer-gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF-target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Topological centrality prioritized master transcriptional drivers governing TNBC oncogenic signaling, including CTCF, POLR2A, EP300, JUND, MYC, and FOS, which regulate Hallmark programs for Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (p = 1.2 x 10-9) and cell cycle progression. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). In silico-simulated driver feature silencing correlated with experimental responses (R2 = 0.473, p < 10-122), and master driver signatures significantly stratified overall survival in the METABRIC (n = 320) and TCGA-BRCA (n = 160; p [≤] 0.019) cohorts. Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

title: Confidence-Guided Machine Learning Staging of the Mouse Estrous Cycle from External Anatomical Images Reduces Cytology Burden
summary: Although the 2015 National Institutes of Health mandate to consider sex as a biological variable in preclinical studies has increased sex-inclusive study designs, many research groups continue to cite the complexity of monitoring female-specific physiology as a barrier to adoption. Central to this challenge is the murine estrous cycle, a hormonally driven process comprising four stages (proestrus, estrus, metestrus, and diestrus), each associated with distinct hormonal and cytological profiles. Current staging methods rely primarily on vaginal cytology, which requires skilled animal handling, specialized expertise in cytology observation, and considerable time, limiting their routine application outside of reproductive endocrinology. To address these barriers, we developed and evaluated a machine learning framework for estrous cycle staging based on photographs of the mouse external vaginal opening. Using 2,297 photographs from C57BL/6J and BALB/c female mice paired with concurrent cytological assessments and partitioned strictly at the animal level, we trained and evaluated three models of varying granularity: a four-stage model, a three-stage model combining metestrus and diestrus, and a two-stage binary model separating the follicular from the luteal and transitional phases. In a held-out evaluation cohort of 466 photographs from 29 unseen mice, overall classification accuracy was 47.4% (95% CI: 40.7-51.9%) for the four-stage model, 54.5% (47.6-62.9%) for the three-group model, and 69.5% (61.8-75.3%) for the binary two-group model. Misclassifications occurred predominantly between biologically adjacent stages, particularly between proestrus and estrus. Crucially, applying a calibrated confidence threshold to the two-group classifier increased accuracy to 82.8% (95% CI: 71.1-92.1%) among the 43.8% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.80, and to 92.5% (95% CI: 87.1-96.6%) among the 20.0% of photographs with confidence [≥] 0.90. While external photography does not support standalone four-stage classification, confidence-guided photographic assessment offers an accessible decision-support framework to selectively triage uncertain cases for cytology and reduce the wet-lab burden of estrous monitoring in preclinical research, including cohort assembly for hormone-dependent models of genital tract infection.

title: Small but Mighty: The Surprising Metabolic Range of a Bacterial Microcompartment
summary: Bacterial microcompartments (BMCs) are protein-based metabolic modules increasingly investigat-ed as potential intracellular nanoreactors. In this study, we engineered Escherichia coli by chromo-somally integrating the propanediol utilization (pdu) operon from Citrobacter freundii and evaluat-ed the metabolic versatility of the heterologously produced Pdu BMCs. The formation of well-assembled, operational Pdu BMCs was confirmed in cellula. Oxygen was found to inhibit 1,2-propanediol utilization, an effect alleviated under microaerobic conditions. The engineered E. coli strain assimilated a range of diols and triols, demonstrating that Pdu BMCs process both their native substrate and glycerol and linear diols up to 1,2-butanediol (C4). This substrate promiscuity was exploited to produce high value-added compounds and revealed previously unrecognized potential for plastic upcycling through ethylene glycol metabolism. In keeping with molecular dynamics simu-lations indicating that the Pdu BMC shell does not impose significant diffusion barriers for longer chain diols and triols, the range of amenable substrates was successfully extended to 1,2-pentanediol (C5) by mutating the diol dehydratase large subunit (PduC). Finally, deletion of pduPQ revealed that host metabolism partially compensated for the loss of BMC-associated aldehyde-processing enzymes, but did not reach the conversion efficiency and product distribution support-ed by the intact Pdu system. Together, these findings establish heterologous Pdu BMCs as promis-cuous and genetically tunable metabolic modules in E. coli, highlighting their potential as scalable platforms for synthetic biology and biotechnological applications.

title: RAxML-NG 2: Automatic model selection, novel tree search heuristics, and fast branch support metrics
summary: RAxML-NG is a widely used tool for maximum likelihood based phylogenetic inference. In the seven years since the last RAxML-NG publication, we have continuously improved and extended the code. Here, we describe the next major release, RAxML-NG 2.0. It introduces a plethora of new features: integrated model testing, multiple fast branch support metrics, automatic parallelization tuning, phylogenetic difficulty prediction, genotype evolution models, to name but the most important ones. Furthermore, we introduce two novel search heuristics at production code level: the adaptive difficulty-aware heuristic (default) and the fast mode with early-stopping that prevents over-optimization. We perform extensive benchmarking of RAxML-NG 2.0 with respect to its accuracy and speed, and compare it to other popular maximum likelihood based phylogenetic inference tools (IQTree, VeryFastTree) as well as to preceding RAxML-NG versions. In particular, the new fast search heuristic in conjunction with machine learning based branch support prediction induces a 75x inference time reduction compared to RAxML-NG 1.2, with minor to no accuracy loss. The code is available under GNU GPL at https://codeberg.org/amkozlov/raxml-ng.

title: Molecular dynamics simulations and in vivo binding studies indicate distinct membrane binding modes of plant lipid droplet proteins including binding via a hydrophobic face
summary: Plant lipid droplets (LDs) are specialized cellular subcompartments for lipid storage and key hubs for lipid metabolism. They have a unique structure: a hydrophobic core composed of neutral lipids enclosed by a phospholipid monolayer and associated proteins. Progress has been made in the identification and characterization of LD-associated plant proteins in recent years, raising the question of how these proteins bind to LDs. To investigate common structural features of LD association, we set up an in silico system using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the nature of this interaction and to identify predicted binding regions of selected proteins. We then tested the importance of these regions for LD association by transient expression of truncated or mutated variants in tobacco pollen tubes. With this combined approach, we investigated the LD targeting region of thirteen LD-associated proteins. In several proteins, a distinct structural feature, a hydrophobic face, binds to LDs by interacting with the acyl chains of the phospholipid monolayer through large hydrophobic residues thereby pushing the headgroups to the sides. We also analyzed proteins previously assayed for LD association and demonstrate a correlation between predicted binding parameters and in vivo binding.
